basic_information.name: Anthropic Claude Code / Agent SDK
basic_information.creator: Anthropic (founded 2021 by Dario Amodei, Daniela Amodei, and former OpenAI researchers)
basic_information.release_date: Claude Code: February 2025 (research preview), May 2025 (GA with Claude 4). Agent SDK: October 2025 (open-source release alongside Claude Sonnet 4.5)
basic_information.license: Claude Code: proprietary (source-available on GitHub but governed by Anthropic's Commercial Terms of Service). Agent SDK: proprietary (source-available, governed by Anthropic's Commercial Terms of Service). Not open-source under OSI-approved licenses like MIT or Apache 2.0.
basic_information.current_version: Claude Code: v2.1.37 (February 2026). Agent SDK (Python): v0.1.33 (February 7, 2026). Agent SDK also available as TypeScript (@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk on npm).

technical_architecture.architecture_pattern: single_agent | orchestrator | code_first — Claude Code is a terminal-native agentic coding tool operating as a single agent with an orchestrator harness. The Agent SDK exposes the same harness for building custom agents. The architecture follows a feedback loop: gather context -> take action -> verify work -> repeat. Supports subagents (child agent instances spawned by the main agent for focused subtasks) and background tasks for long-running operations. The 'agent harness' acts as an operating system that curates the context window, handles prompts and hooks, and exposes tools and skills.
technical_architecture.underlying_models: Built exclusively on Anthropic Claude models. Currently supports Claude Opus 4.6 (latest, with agent teams research preview), Claude Opus 4.5, Claude Sonnet 4.5 (default model), and Claude Haiku 4.5. Not model-agnostic — tightly coupled to the Claude model family. Context window up to 200,000 tokens input with output capacities up to 128,000 tokens.
technical_architecture.tool_integration: Native MCP (Model Context Protocol) support — Claude Code can connect to any MCP server (stdio and SSE). Built-in tools: Bash (sandboxed), Read (file reading), Write (file writing), Edit (precise string replacement), Glob (file search), Grep (content search), WebFetch (URL content), WebSearch (web search), NotebookEdit (Jupyter notebooks). Agent SDK supports custom tools via Python @tool decorator (implemented as in-process MCP servers). Pre-configured OAuth client credentials for MCP servers like Slack. Supports hundreds or thousands of tools across dozens of MCP servers simultaneously.
technical_architecture.planning_approach: code_as_plan | ReAct — Claude Code uses an agentic loop where the model reasons about the task, selects and executes tools, observes results, and iterates. Plan mode available for explicit planning before execution. Subagents allow hierarchical task decomposition. No formal tree-of-thought or graph-based planning — the model itself drives planning through its reasoning capabilities. Skills system allows pre-defined workflows with forked context and hot-reload.
technical_architecture.multi_agent_support: Yes — multiple patterns. (1) Subagents: separate agent instances spawned by the main agent for focused subtasks with isolated context windows, can run concurrently. (2) Agent Teams: research preview feature in Claude Opus 4.6 for multi-agent collaboration. (3) Background agents: long-running autonomous agents working independently. (4) Via Agent SDK: developers can orchestrate multiple agents programmatically. Subagents can be configured with specialized instructions, tools, and permissions.

memory_and_context.memory_types_supported: short_term | semantic | procedural — (1) Short-term: conversation history within a session. (2) Semantic/procedural: CLAUDE.md files at project (./CLAUDE.md), user (~/.claude/CLAUDE.md), and enterprise levels store persistent instructions, conventions, and learned patterns. (3) Automatic memory: Claude automatically records and recalls memories as it works, persisting insights across sessions. (4) Skills: reusable, modular capability definitions stored as files, functioning as procedural memory.
memory_and_context.context_window_management: Sophisticated multi-strategy approach. (1) Automatic summarization: older messages are summarized when approaching context limits, ensuring long-running agents stay within the model's window. (2) Context editing: automatically removes stale tool calls and results (29% improvement in performance). (3) 'Summarize from here' feature for partial conversation summarization. (4) Subagent isolation: offloading subtasks to subagents with their own context windows prevents main context bloat. (5) PDF handling: large PDFs return lightweight references instead of being inlined. Combined context management delivers 39% improvement in agentic search performance.
memory_and_context.persistence_mechanism: file_system — Memory persists primarily via the filesystem. CLAUDE.md files store project/user/org instructions. ~/.claude/ directory stores user-level settings, memories, and configurations. .claude/settings.json stores permission rules. Skills stored as files with frontmatter. Session state can be teleported to claude.ai. No built-in database or vector store — persistence is file-based and git-friendly.
memory_and_context.context_engineering_approach: Context is a first-class architectural concern in Claude Code. The 'agent harness' explicitly curates context like an operating system managing RAM. Multiple layers: (1) System prompt with tool descriptions and capabilities. (2) CLAUDE.md files loaded at boot (project, user, enterprise levels). (3) .claude/rules/ directory for modular instruction files. (4) Skills frontmatter for task-specific context. (5) Automatic memory for cross-session learning. (6) Dynamic context editing to remove stale information. Anthropic spent 6+ months solving how agents should manage memory across long-running tasks.

capabilities.core_capabilities: Terminal-native agentic coding with natural language commands. Full codebase understanding and navigation. File reading, writing, and precise editing with string replacement. Bash command execution (sandboxed). Git workflow automation (commits, PRs, branch management). Web search and URL content fetching. Jupyter notebook editing. PDF reading with page ranges. Plan mode for complex task planning. Subagents for parallel subtask execution. Background tasks for long-running operations. Skills system for reusable modular capabilities with hot-reload. Hooks for intercepting and controlling agent behavior (PreToolUse, PostToolUse, SubagentStop). Session management with teleport to claude.ai. VS Code extension (beta). GitHub Actions integration via claude-code-action. Agent SDK for building custom agents with the same infrastructure. Multi-agent collaboration (research preview). Automatic memory recording and recall. MCP server connectivity for external tools and data sources. OAuth integration for authenticated services. Image reading (multimodal). 176 updates shipped in 2025.
capabilities.supported_modalities: Text, code, file system, terminal/bash, git, web search, URL fetching, vision (image reading), PDF reading, Jupyter notebooks. MCP enables extension to any data source (Slack, Google Drive, Figma, databases, etc.).
capabilities.autonomy_level: human_in_loop | supervised | copilot — Configurable across a spectrum. Default: permission prompts for potentially risky operations. Sandboxed mode: autonomous within filesystem and network boundaries, reduces permission prompts by 84%. Full autonomous mode possible with pre-configured allow rules. Agent SDK provides programmatic control over autonomy levels. Background agents can work fully autonomously within defined boundaries.
capabilities.tool_ecosystem: Built-in tools: Bash, Read, Write, Edit, Glob, Grep, WebFetch, WebSearch, NotebookEdit. Extensible via MCP: thousands of community-built MCP servers available (Slack, GitHub, Google Drive, Figma, Jira, Asana, databases, monitoring tools, etc.). Pre-configured OAuth for services like Slack. Custom tools via Agent SDK @tool decorator. GitHub Actions integration. VS Code extension. JetBrains IDE integration. Apple Xcode 26.3 native integration. Compatible with the broader MCP ecosystem which has become the de-facto standard for agent-to-tool connectivity.

agent_interoperability.mcp_support: Yes — MCP is a core pillar. Claude Code natively supports connecting to MCP servers (stdio and SSE). Anthropic created and maintains the MCP standard (launched November 2024). The Agent SDK implements custom tools as in-process MCP servers. MCP health checks available for monitoring server status. Thousands of community MCP servers available.
agent_interoperability.a2a_support: Not natively built-in. Google's A2A protocol can be bridged via third-party MCP servers (e.g., A2A-MCP-Server) that allow Claude to discover, register, and communicate with A2A agents. MCP and A2A are complementary: MCP handles agent-to-tool communication, A2A handles agent-to-agent communication. No first-party A2A integration from Anthropic as of February 2026.
agent_interoperability.agents_md_support: No — Claude Code uses its own CLAUDE.md format rather than the cross-tool AGENTS.md standard. CLAUDE.md files are read automatically at session start from project, user, and enterprise levels. AGENTS.md is not supported by default, but can be referenced from within CLAUDE.md as a workaround. Additionally, .claude/rules/ directory supports modular instruction files.
agent_interoperability.cross_framework_compatibility: Moderate. Strong interoperability via MCP (any MCP-compatible framework can share tools). Agent SDK available in Python and TypeScript for embedding in custom systems. Apple Xcode 26.3 natively integrates the Agent SDK. JetBrains IDEs support Claude Agent. Microsoft Semantic Kernel interoperability documented. GitHub integration (claude-code-action). However, tightly coupled to Claude models (no model-agnostic support) which limits framework flexibility compared to model-agnostic alternatives like CrewAI or LangGraph.

safety_and_guardrails.permission_model: allow_list | deny_list | capability_based | sandbox — Multi-layered permission system. Three granular levels: Allow (autonomous), Ask (requires user approval), Deny (blocked). Tool and bash command permissions configurable via glob patterns (e.g., 'allow all npm commands', 'block any command with sudo'). Sandboxed bash uses OS-level primitives: Linux bubblewrap and macOS seatbelt for filesystem and network isolation. Static analysis runs before bash commands to identify risky operations. Organization-level policies can be enforced across all users. Sandboxing reduces permission prompts by 84%.
safety_and_guardrails.escalation_policy: Automatic escalation when actions cross permission boundaries. If Claude attempts to access resources outside the sandbox, the user is notified immediately and can choose to allow or deny. Commands modifying system files or accessing sensitive directories require explicit approval. Permission modes configurable per project via .claude/settings.json. Agent SDK provides a runtime callback for handling permission requests programmatically.
safety_and_guardrails.hallucination_mitigation: Multiple strategies. (1) Tool-grounded verification: Claude Code can run code, execute tests, and verify outputs against actual runtime behavior, creating a verify-before-commit loop. (2) Chain-of-thought reasoning visible in plan mode. (3) Subagent cross-verification: multiple subagents can independently validate results. (4) File-system grounding: Claude reads actual code rather than relying on memory. (5) Web search for fact-checking. (6) Skills with knowledge bases that can be corrected via feedback loops. (7) Structured outputs constrain responses. (8) Official Anthropic guidance recommends extracting verbatim quotes before analysis and citing sources.
safety_and_guardrails.audit_trail: Yes — comprehensive. OpenTelemetry native support exports events: user prompts (claude_code.user_prompt), tool completions (claude_code.tool_result), API requests (claude_code.api_request), API errors (claude_code.api_error). Token usage and cost tracked per interaction via modelUsage. Hooks (PreToolUse, PostToolUse) provide event capture at lifecycle points. Session history persisted and browsable via claude.ai.
safety_and_guardrails.human_oversight_pattern: pre-approval | confidence_threshold | always_on — Default: ask-before-risky-action (pre-approval for destructive operations). Sandbox mode: autonomous within boundaries, escalate on boundary crossing (confidence_threshold pattern). Configurable to always-ask or fully autonomous via permission rules. Agent SDK provides callback-based oversight at runtime. Enterprise organizations can set policies enforced across all users.

governance_and_standards.governance_body: Anthropic (private company, no external standards body governance). MCP (Model Context Protocol) is Anthropic-created but open-standard, adopted broadly by the industry. No AAIF or Linux Foundation governance over Claude Code itself.
governance_and_standards.contributing_protocols: Creator and maintainer of MCP (Model Context Protocol) — the de-facto industry standard for agent-to-tool connectivity, adopted by OpenAI, Google, Microsoft, Apple, and thousands of community developers. OpenTelemetry support for observability. OAuth 2.0 for authenticated MCP server connections. JSON-RPC for MCP communication.
governance_and_standards.regulatory_compliance: Anthropic holds SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certifications. ISO/IEC 42001:2023 for AI management systems. HIPAA-configurable with Business Associate Agreement (BAA) available for qualifying customers. EU AI Act: Anthropic engages with regulatory bodies and conducts risk assessments, but no explicit EU AI Act certification publicly documented. Claude Code sandboxing and permission model support compliance workflows.

deployment_and_operations.deployment_modes: local | cloud | hybrid — Claude Code runs locally in the terminal (primary mode). VS Code extension for IDE integration. GitHub Actions for CI/CD (cloud). Agent SDK supports cloud deployment for custom agent applications. Session teleport between terminal and claude.ai (hybrid). Apple Xcode integration (local IDE). JetBrains IDE integration (local). API-based usage via Claude API for cloud deployments.
deployment_and_operations.scalability_model: serverless | horizontal — Claude Code itself is a single-user CLI tool. Scales via API (Anthropic handles model serving). Agent SDK agents scale via standard application scaling patterns. Batch processing API available for high-volume workloads. Background agents and subagents enable concurrent task execution. GitHub Actions integration provides CI/CD-scale agent deployment. Enterprise API supports high-volume usage with custom rate limits.
deployment_and_operations.cost_per_task: Consumption-based API pricing. Claude Sonnet 4.5 (default): $3/$15 per million tokens (input/output). Claude Opus 4.5: $5/$25 per million tokens. Claude Haiku 4.5: $1/$5 per million tokens. Prompt caching reduces input costs by up to 90% on cache hits. Batch processing: $0.50/$2.50 per million tokens (Opus). Long context (>200K input tokens): $6/$22.50 per million tokens. Typical coding task (file edit + test): roughly $0.05-$0.50 depending on complexity and model. Complex multi-file refactoring: $1-$10+. Consumer plans: Pro ($10/month, 300 premium requests), Pro+ ($39/month, 1,500 premium requests), Max plan for heaviest usage.
deployment_and_operations.resource_requirements: Lightweight — runs as a Node.js CLI application locally. Requires: Node.js runtime, internet connection for API calls, Anthropic API key or Claude subscription. No GPU required (model inference runs on Anthropic's cloud). Minimal local compute — the heavy lifting happens server-side. Works on Linux, macOS, and Windows. Docker support available for containerized environments.

observability_and_ops.monitoring_integration: Native OpenTelemetry (OTel) support for metrics and events. Compatible with: Langfuse, LangSmith (LangChain), Arize (Dev-Agent-Lens), SigNoz, Honeycomb, Datadog, Sentry, Logfire, Grafana, Prometheus, ClickHouse, Elasticsearch, Loki. Claude telemetry wrapper (claudia) available as drop-in replacement. MLflow autolog support for the Agent SDK. Configured via environment variables (CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY=1).
observability_and_ops.tracing_support: Yes — detailed execution traces available via OpenTelemetry. Traces include: user prompts, tool calls with parameters, API requests/responses, token usage, costs, and execution timing. Langfuse and LangSmith provide visual trace exploration. Hooks (PreToolUse, PostToolUse) enable custom trace points. Subagent traces correlatable via tool_use_id. OpenInference standard (built on OpenTelemetry) for rich LLM observability.
observability_and_ops.production_readiness_level: production_ready — Claude Code has shipped 176 updates in 2025 alone, progressing from research preview to production tool. v2.1.x series focuses on enterprise infrastructure (skills hot-reload, task management, keyboard customization). Agent SDK actively used in production by Apple (Xcode 26.3), JetBrains, and enterprise customers. Used internally at Anthropic for their own development. However, the Agent SDK is still at v0.1.x indicating ongoing API stabilization.

human_agent_interaction.autonomy_spectrum: copilot (suggestions) | assistant (executes with approval) | autonomous (acts independently) — Full spectrum configurable. Default: assistant mode with permission prompts for risky actions. Sandbox mode: autonomous within defined boundaries. Background agents: fully autonomous for long-running tasks. Agent SDK: programmatic control over autonomy level. Plan mode: copilot-style where Claude proposes before executing.
human_agent_interaction.handoff_mechanism: Permission prompts pause execution and request user decision (allow/deny/always allow). Plan mode presents proposed actions for review before execution. If sandbox boundaries are crossed, immediate user notification with allow/deny choice. Session teleport allows handing off from terminal to claude.ai web interface. VS Code extension enables IDE-based interaction. Agent SDK provides callback functions for programmatic handoff logic. Subagent failures escalate to the parent agent.
human_agent_interaction.feedback_loop: Automatic memory: Claude records insights and recalls them in future sessions, creating a persistent learning loop. CLAUDE.md files serve as explicit human-edited feedback that shapes agent behavior across all sessions. Skills knowledge bases can be updated with corrections. Project-level .claude/rules/ allow incremental refinement. No built-in RLHF or automated fine-tuning from user feedback — improvements come through: (1) automatic memory accumulation, (2) CLAUDE.md refinement, (3) model upgrades from Anthropic, (4) skills/hooks configuration.

entrepreneurial_relevance.startup_applicability: Very high applicability for technical startups and developer-heavy teams. USE WHEN: (1) Your team builds software and wants to accelerate development velocity, (2) You need an AI coding agent integrated into existing terminal/git workflows, (3) You want to build custom AI agents for your product using the Agent SDK, (4) You need MCP-based tool integration for connecting AI to your data sources, (5) You want the strongest safety and permission model for regulated industries. AVOID WHEN: (1) Your team is non-technical — Claude Code is terminal-first, not GUI-first, (2) You need model-agnostic flexibility — Claude Code only works with Claude models, (3) You are building multi-agent workflows with agents from different providers — consider LangGraph or CrewAI instead, (4) Budget is extremely constrained — $10-200/month per developer adds up for large teams vs. free alternatives like Goose or Aider. STARTUP STRATEGY: Start with Claude Pro ($10/month) for individual developers, scale to API usage as you build Agent SDK-powered features into your product. The Agent SDK lets you ship Claude-powered features to your customers using the same battle-tested infrastructure Anthropic uses internally.
entrepreneurial_relevance.build_vs_buy: BUY (use Claude Code) when: you want best-in-class coding assistance, your team already uses terminal workflows, and you value strong safety guardrails. BUILD (use Agent SDK) when: you want to embed Claude's agent capabilities into your own product, need custom tools/workflows, or want programmatic control over agent behavior. ALTERNATIVE frameworks: LangGraph for model-agnostic multi-agent orchestration, CrewAI for role-based multi-agent teams, AutoGen for research-heavy conversation workflows. Cost comparison: Claude Code Pro ($10/mo) vs. Cursor Pro ($20/mo) vs. GitHub Copilot Individual ($10/mo) vs. free alternatives (Goose, Aider). The Agent SDK differentiates by being both a development tool AND a platform for building AI-powered products.
